- Second largest player in the Indian tile industry

- Brand equity built on VC Shield - patented, Superbrands-recognised and awarded the Corporate Technical Achievement Award by the American Ceramic Society
- Government-recognised in-house R&D facility and a record of firsts (first CONTINUA+ plant, first glazed vitrified tile facility)

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Subdued domestic demand — The Board's Report states the Company continued to face a challenging business environment marked by subdued market demand, with weak demand conditions especially in the first half of the financial year - a direct constraint on volume growth and operating leverage.
- Export headwinds from anti-dumping duties — The industry's growth dynamics are shifting as exports face challenges from anti-dumping duties imposed by key markets such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Taiwan, pushing Indian manufacturers to refocus domestically.
- Energy and emissions management in an energy-intensive process — Identified in the BRSR as a material risk: rising energy costs, growing expectations for energy reporting and disclosure, and increasingly stringent emissions regulation create long-term risk from inefficient resource use in energy-intensive operations, requiring strategic planning and continuous improvement.
- Water scarcity, regulation and stewardship — Identified in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity: limited availability of water resources, growing water scarcity, increasingly stringent regulations and potential reputational impacts from unsustainable water use; ineffective water management in tile manufacturing can raise operational and regulatory costs and disrupt supply.
- Product concentration in tiles — BRSR business-activity disclosure shows ceramic/vitrified wall and floor tiles account for 83.47% of turnover, with sanitaryware and bath fittings at 12.02%, leaving results heavily levered to a single category.
- Domestic market concentration / limited export diversification — Exports contribute only 2.74% of total turnover, so the revenue base is almost entirely dependent on Indian construction and renovation demand.
- Macro and policy dependence on the construction cycle — Demand outlook is explicitly tied to GDP growth, government infrastructure spending, urbanization and real-estate activity; the Company itself notes moderation in projected FY 2026-27 GDP growth due to geopolitical uncertainties and energy-related risks.
- Employee attrition and talent retention — BRSR turnover-rate disclosure shows the permanent-employee attrition rate rose to 12.68% in FY 2025-26 from 11.90% in FY 2024-25 and 11.78% in FY 2023-24; the ESOP disclosures also record options lapsing during the year due to resignations of eligible employees.

business.body: Somany Ceramics Limited manufactures and trades ceramic and vitrified wall and floor tiles, glazed vitrified tiles, digital tiles, tile adhesives and construction solutions, along with sanitaryware and bath fittings. The portfolio serves both residential and commercial spaces, and the Company describes tiles as the foundation of its business and the starting point of its design story. Customers span retailers, distributors, builders, contractors and end users across domestic and international markets.

outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body: Increasing demand for ceramic products in India; Growing infrastructure development
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Transition from a traditional ceramic tile manufacturer into a surfaces and building solutions company - a holistic, 360-degree surface and space solutions provider
- Strategically expand into high-potential adjacencies that complement the core - sanitaryware, bathware, adhesives and building solutions - to participate more meaningfully in the home-building and interior solutions ecosystem
- Entry into construction chemicals and advanced waterproofing through the acquisition of a 51% majority stake in Dura Build Care Private Limited ('Durabuild'), participating earlier in the construction value chain via waterproofing, adhesives and specialised building chemical solutions
- Premiumization - strengthen the premium product portfolio and elevate customer experience through continuous investment in brand building, innovation, design and differentiated offerings to capture a larger share of the premium home and building solutions market
- Expand and deepen the distribution network across existing and new channels, leveraging the combined strengths of the tile, bathware and building solutions businesses to create cross-selling opportunities across the construction lifecycle
- Sharpen focus on operational excellence and capital efficiency - with major capacity investments completed, drive growth through improved capacity utilisation, stronger free cash flow generation and enhanced return ratios under a disciplined capital allocation approach
- Build complementary growth engines alongside the core tile business to diversify revenue streams and expand the addressable market
- Decarbonisation and green energy transition - ramp up open-access solar consumption through the Clean Max Ananta Private Limited investment and institutionalise waste heat recovery systems (WHRS) across production lines
- Resource circularity - maintain zero liquid discharge with closed-loop filtration recirculating 100% of process water, and substitute virgin minerals with recycled ceramic scrap in raw material sourcing
- Maintain a diversified manufacturing footprint across North and South India with prudent inventory planning to keep production and customer supply stable through fuel and gas disruptions
- The Board has recommended a final dividend on the equity shares for the financial year ended 31 March, 2026 for adoption by members at the 58th Annual General Meeting, alongside adoption of the standalone and consolidated financial statements. No separate dividend distribution policy statement, buyback, debt-reduction or credit-rating intent is set out in the routed governance text; the only other capital-related item placed before members is approval of material related-party transactions with Sudha Somany Ceramics Private Limited, subject to a stated monetary cap and the Company's Policy on Related Party Transactions.
- Both the Kadi and Kassar facilities operate as Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) units, with 100% of wastewater generated treated and reused within operations and no discharge into the environment
- Three effluent treatment plants (ETPs) installed to enable complete reuse of treated water in manufacturing processes
- Annual Canal Water Agreement secured for raw water supply, reducing reliance on groundwater
- No Objection Certificate obtained from the Central Ground Water Authority (CGWA) for groundwater extraction, with a fresh application submitted to the Haryana Water Resource Authority to maintain compliance
- Regular water quality testing of ETP and STP outputs through NABL-accredited laboratories
- A recent government-authorized water audit commended the effectiveness of the ZLD system
- Renovation of toilet facilities with pipeline redesign to reduce domestic water consumption
- Additional water measures: reuse of cooling tower blowdown water, prioritising recycled water over fresh water across operations, leak detection and timely repairs, and setting targeted water conservation goals supported by actionable strategies
- Energy and emissions management recognised as a critical risk area requiring strategic planning and continuous improvement to navigate evolving regulatory and financial challenges
- Grievance redressal mechanism established with policies aligned to each of the nine NGRBC principles, enabling stakeholders across communities, investors, shareholders, employees, customers and value-chain partners to raise concerns
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company's access to tile capacity remained at ~75 msm, comprising 31.65 msm from its own plants, 25 msm from subsidiaries and associates and ~18 msm through other outsourcing arrangements; the R&D disclosure separately describes the combined capacity as ~75 million square metres per annum. In the Bathware segment, the Company through its subsidiaries had capacity of 0.48 million pieces per annum of sanitaryware and 1.30 million pieces per annum of bath fittings. The Company states it continued to invest in the expansion and upgradation of its manufacturing facilities, plant and machinery and infrastructure. Named capability additions during the year include a newly commissioned polishing and squaring line covering a 20,000 sq m area aimed at high-speed precision and industrial-scale consistency of polished products, and a state-of-the-art digital printing machine from System, Italy installed in synchronisation with the existing digital machine, which can produce structured effects on the tile surface without maintaining an inventory of punches, eliminating traditional punch changes and improving throughput. On the product side the Company incorporated 12 mm GVT thickness for high-traffic zones. Energy-related asset additions include rooftop solar power plants at the Kassar and Kadi facilities, which generated approximately 37.65 lakh units of renewable energy during the year, plus approximately 15.65 lakh units of solar power procured under the group captive model for the Kadi plant; waste heat from kilns was recovered and used in horizontal dryers, and VFDs, IE3 motors, BEE-certified LED lighting and APFC-equipped capacitors were installed, with energy-saving projects delivering estimated annual savings of approximately 2.92 lakh kWh. The manufacturing footprint referenced in the Corporate Overview is 10 plants across India, with own tile units at Kassar, Haryana (25.00 msm) and Kadi, Gujarat (6.65 msm) and further tile capacity held through Somany Piastrelle (4.50 msm), Somany Max (4.00 msm), Sudha Somany Ceramics (8.40 msm), Vintage Tiles (5.40 msm) and Vicon Ceramics (2.64 msm), alongside bathware units at Somany Bath Fittings (1.30 million pieces) and Somany Sanitary Ware (0.48 million pieces). No new named greenfield project with a forward commissioning date is disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- A robust residential real estate up-cycle, supported by government initiatives, infrastructure investments and Smart City development, creating sustained demand for ceramic tiles and allied products
- Rising disposable incomes and improving living standards accelerating renovation and home modernization activity as an additional growth avenue
- Consumers increasingly embracing premium, large-format GVT and porcelain slabs, expanding the addressable market for value-added products and creating opportunities for higher-margin growth
- India's rapid urbanization and infrastructure expansion viewed by management as a multi-decade structural growth cycle for the ceramic and building materials industry
- Gas supply and price volatility - Middle-East geopolitical tensions constrained fuel availability and drove a sharp rise in gas prices from early March, hitting propane-dependent units in the Morbi cluster and necessitating calibrated industry-wide price revisions
- A challenging export environment with elevated logistics costs and structural realignment across key international markets contributing to a slowdown in export volumes
- Non-tile categories - sanitaryware, bathware and building solutions - growing at healthy double-digit rates and emerging as meaningful contributors that broaden the revenue base and reduce dependence on any single product category
- India's domestic waterproofing / building solutions market treated as a structural multiplier to the core surfaces business, with the Durabuild integration adding specialised SKUs and deeper builder and project-developer engagement
- Continued focus on product mix optimisation as a margin lever
- A cleaner balance sheet and stronger cash flows described by management as the platform for the next phase of growth
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Somany Ceramics Limited is a leading manufacturer of ceramic products with a strong presence in the Indian market, and its credit rating reaffirmation by CRISIL reflects its stable financial position and growth prospects. The company's focus on sustainable building materials and infrastructure development is expected to drive its growth in the future. With a strong brand presence and a wide distribution network, Somany Ceramics is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for ceramic products in India.

open.item: Complete the sale of the Company's entire equity stake in associate Acer Granito Private Limited under the Share Purchase Agreement, with the completion timeline mutually extended by a further nine months.

Grow presence across adjacent categories - sanitaryware, bath fittings, building solutions and integrated decor - to deliver comprehensive, end-to-end solutions for contemporary living and commercial environments.

With significant capacity investments completed, drive future growth through improved capacity utilization, stronger free cash flow generation and enhanced return ratios while maintaining disciplined capital allocation.

Anchor strategy on premiumization by strengthening the premium product portfolio and investing in brand building, innovation and design to capture a larger share of the premium home and building solutions market.

Continue expanding and strengthening the distribution network across existing and new channels to improve accessibility and create cross-selling opportunities across tile, bathware and building solutions.

Management flags constrained fuel availability and a sharp increase in gas prices from early March following Middle-East geopolitical tensions, which had a pronounced impact on propane-dependent units in the Morbi ceramic cluster.
